description: Music Years 5-6 width tiers — ACARA v9. All strands are capability strands; width axis is task_contexts throughout.
subject: Music

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single musical context that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term. For Y5-6, minimum is typically one task demonstrating the key capability (manipulate elements + compositional devices, develop aural/instrumental skills, perform, explore).
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope across the most common elaboration cases. Reflects a well-taught Y5-6 class engaging with multiple composition, performance and exploration contexts including digital tools.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts — different styles, audiences, technologies, cultural settings or collaborative purposes. First Nations contexts included where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. E02 descriptor is entirely First Nations-focused and its elaborations are the primary framing for that entry.

AC9AMU6C01.minimum_width: Compose a piece that uses at least one compositional device (e.g. repetition, contrast, or a given form such as verse/chorus) and manipulates at least two elements of music to communicate an idea; notate, document or record the work.
AC9AMU6C01.typical_width: Manipulate elements of music and use compositional devices across multiple creation contexts — composing in response to an image, theme or question; arranging or re-imagining known works; using digital tools to combine loops with live performance; composing for specific instruments within a limited pitch range; notating using graphic/staff notation or audio recording; composing music for cross-curricular presentations or for specific cultural purposes.
wider: Work collaboratively to compose a song for a cross-curricular presentation (e.g. History or English) — write lyrics, create a chord progression and arrange for available instruments and voices
Arrange or re-imagine a known work with new lyrics and instrumentation — document the choices made and explain how the re-imagining reflects a particular style or audience
Use digital tools (loop software, notation apps) to combine constructed loops with live instrumental or vocal performance — create a multi-layer composition
Compose a song, chant or soundscape for a specific cultural purpose (e.g. an Acknowledgement of Country or a Welcome to Country) using correct protocols and with appropriate guidance
elaborations: working collaboratively to compose music in response to an image, theme or question
improvising and experimenting with combinations of sounds and/or using digital tools to create moods and atmospheres
rehearsing a range of unison and part music individually and/or in an ensemble
using a limited range of pitches to compose melodies for a selected instrument
arranging or re-imagining a known work; for example, writing new lyrics and arranging for available instruments
composing a melody, manipulating elements of music such as rhythm, pitch, dynamics, texture or timbre, and using a compositional device/s to structure the music
using voice/vocalisation and sounds such as body percussion or drumming to develop a song, chant or soundscape for a Welcome to Country or Acknowledgement of Country
using digital tools, voices and instruments to compose, notate, document and/or record music

AC9AMU6D01.minimum_width: Demonstrate one vocal or instrumental skill focused on a specific element of music (e.g. improvising a short melody, or adjusting own volume when singing in a group); use listening to evaluate and refine.
AC9AMU6D01.typical_width: Develop listening/aural skills and skills for manipulating elements of music across solo and ensemble contexts — combining listening and performance (adjusting volume for balance), exploring vocal/instrumental techniques to create contrast and repetition, setting goals from listening observations, using digital tools (tuner, metronome, recording software) to develop accuracy and control; practise techniques for solo and ensemble music.
wider: Use digital tools (tuner, notation software, dynamic range monitor) to systematically build technical control — set measurable goals, track progress and document improvement
Develop ensemble balance skills in a small group — focus on hearing and adjusting to other parts in real time, and describe how the ensemble sound changes with different volume balances
Explore how timbre manipulation (changing tone colour of voice or instrument) can create and vary mood — compare techniques used in different musical styles or genres
Use focused listening to a recording of a professional performer to set personal technique goals — identify specific techniques and develop practice strategies to achieve them
elaborations: developing vocal and/or instrumental skills by focusing on specific elements of music; for example, improvising patterns, phrases or melodies
combining listening/aural and performance skills; for example, listening to hear other parts when singing or playing in a group
exploring vocal/instrumental techniques to manipulate elements of music to create contrast, repetition and balance
developing vocal and instrumental skills such as manipulating the timbre of instruments and voices to create and vary mood
using digital tools to build skills such as accuracy and control
practising techniques for singing and playing to develop technical skills in solo and ensemble music

AC9AMU6E01.minimum_width: Listen to music from one cultural context or genre; describe how at least two elements of music are combined and share a personal response with reasons.
AC9AMU6E01.typical_width: Explore ways that elements of music are combined across cultures, times, places and other contexts — listening to diverse instrumentation and forms; evaluating personal preferences for music from multiple contexts; identifying structural features (riffs, strumming patterns, instrumentation) that create effects; listening to and responding to music from Asian and other cultures; considering how music is used in celebrations, ceremonies or rituals; demonstrating understanding of popular song form.
wider: Compare original versions of songs with arrangements, covers or reimaginings — explore how changing instrumentation, tempo or style changes the effect and meaning

Investigate how music is used in celebrations, ceremonies or rituals in two or more cultural contexts (e.g. a school ceremony and a community cultural event) — compare how music gives structure to the occasion
Use parody to demonstrate understanding of popular song structure — compose new lyrics to a known song, justifying how the structure was used
Listen to and respond to music from Asian cultures — discuss what the music communicates, how elements of music are used, and make connections to the composer/performer's context and purpose
elaborations: listening to music that uses a range of instrumentation or forms and describing how the elements of music are used or combined
evaluating and discussing personal preferences for music from a range of contexts and cultures
identifying and describing features of music that create effects, such as ways in which elements of music are manipulated
listening to (and/or performing) and responding to music from a variety of contexts and cultures, such as Asian cultures
considering ways in which music is used in celebrations, ceremonies or rituals
demonstrating understanding of the form and structure of popular songs

AC9AMU6E02.minimum_width: Investigate one way that First Nations Australian composers or performers use music to continue or revitalise culture; share a specific observation about the style, instruments or cultural purpose of the music.
AC9AMU6E02.typical_width: Explore ways First Nations Australians use music to continue and revitalise culture — investigating diverse music styles and instruments used by living composers/performers; investigating how music maintains and revitalises First Nations Australian languages; investigating music created for Dance, Drama, Media Arts or Visual Arts works that share cultural knowledge; investigating how performers share cultural knowledge as part of performances.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian musicians use music to maintain and revitalise specific language groups — explore examples of songs that teach or preserve language knowledge
Investigate how First Nations Australian composers create music for animations or screen-based works that share cultural knowledge about places, birds or animals

Compare how two or more First Nations Australian artists working in different styles (e.g. contemporary pop and ceremonial music) both contribute to continuing culture — what different purposes does each serve?
elaborations: investigating the range of music styles and instruments that living First Nations Australian composers and/or performers are using in their work
investigating how music is being used to maintain and revitalise knowledge and use of First Nations Australian languages
investigating music that First Nations Australian composers are creating for dance, drama, media arts or visual arts works that share cultural knowledge
investigating how First Nations Australian composers and/or performers share knowledge about their culture as part of performances

AC9AMU6P01.minimum_width: Perform one piece in a form they have learnt or composed; demonstrate at least one expressive element (e.g. dynamics or balance) and show awareness of audience.
AC9AMU6P01.typical_width: Perform music in a range of forms in informal and/or formal settings — rehearsing and refining to engage audiences and communicate ideas; providing and responding to feedback to refine performances; presenting performances via digital platforms including school intranet or website; focusing on expressive elements such as dynamics, balance, tone colour and articulation; performing songs from cultural groups or songs in a language being learnt.
wider: Stream or upload a performance recording to a school-managed platform, add discussion questions for the audience, and evaluate the responses received
Perform music from a specific cultural group or in a language being learnt — focus on how expressive elements communicate the mood and cultural context of the music
Provide structured peer feedback on a rehearsal recording using specific music terminology — document the feedback and track how it informs the next rehearsal
elaborations: rehearsing and refining performances to engage audiences and communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
providing and responding to feedback to refine performances and compositions
presenting performances via digital platforms including, if age-appropriate, interacting with audiences via platforms such as school intranet or website
